sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example is written more briefly. Fill in the reasoning it leaves out.

items.prompt: A population has 500 students. Student A takes a random sample of 10. Student B takes a random sample of 50. Both use proper random selection. Whose sample is more likely to give an estimate closer to the true population value?

steps: Both samples are random, so neither is biased by the selection method.
A larger random sample generally has less variability between repeated samples.
Student B's sample of 50 is larger than Student A's sample of 10, so it is more likely to be closer to the true population value.
workedSolution.answer: Student B's sample of 50, because larger random samples tend to produce more consistent, accurate estimates.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A student surveys 49 visitors to a science museum using a simple random sample and records the results. Is it valid to generalize this result to all 1078 visitors to a science museum?
choices: No, because the sample was not randomly selected, so it may not represent the population.
Yes, because the sample was selected randomly, so it is likely representative of the population.
No, because samples can never be generalized to a population.
Yes, because the sample size is large enough regardless of how it was chosen.

items.prompt: A sample of 7 values is: 21, 36, 24, 39, 34, 48, 39. What is the median of this data set?
A data set has 6 values: 35, 37, 37, 36, 35, 37. What is the new mean if an outlier of 90 is added to the data set, making 7 values in all?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A data set is: 6, 13, 6, 12, 43, with a mean of 16. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of this data set?
Two data sets have means of 38 and 54. Their mean absolute deviation (MAD) is 5. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.
choices: 6 2/5 times the MAD
16 times the MAD
4 1/5 times the MAD
3 1/5 times the MAD

items.prompt: Sample A: 34, 38, 25, 42, 18, 35. Sample B: 60, 63, 64, 69, 45, 35. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?
choices: Both samples have the same mean.
Sample B, with a mean of 32 compared to 56.
Sample A, with a mean of 32 compared to 56.
Sample B, with a mean of 56 compared to 32.

items.prompt: Sample A: 22, 20, 21, 21, 20, 21. Sample B: 29, 15, 33, 24, 32, 25. Based on the range of each sample, which sample is more consistent (less variable)?
choices: Sample A, with a range of 18 compared to 2.
Both samples have the same range.
Sample A, with a range of 2 compared to 18.
Sample B, with a range of 18 compared to 2.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 1726 commuters on a train line. She randomly selects 256 of them to survey. What is the sample in this situation?
choices: The researcher's own estimate
The 256 randomly selected commuters on a train line
All 1726 commuters on a train line
Only the first 256 commuters on a train line on a list

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A student picks a random starting point, then surveys every 10th person from the full numbered list of visitors to a science museum, for a total of 69. Is this sampling method likely to produce a representative sample?
choices: No, likely not representative, because the population is too large.
No, likely not representative — the method favors certain members over others.
Yes, likely representative — every member had a fair, known chance of being chosen.
Yes, likely representative, because the sample size is large enough.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 40 commuters on a train line, 23 preferred an extended weekend event. Based on this sample, about how many of the 160 commuters on a train line would you expect to prefer an extended weekend event?
